title: Third Presbyterian Church v. Evangel Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC ruled the complaint not judicially in order (SJC Manual 11.5.d) for lack of jurisdiction; it made no merits ruling on the five complaint grounds or on Presbytery's 38-17 denial.
first_summary: Third Presbyterian Church complained to the SJC after Evangel Presbytery denied its challenge to a Presbytery commission's binding arbitration award of $57,000 to Covenant Classical School. The SJC denied the complaint as not judicially in order, holding that PCA courts cannot act as civil arbitrators or review binding arbitration judgments. It distinguished permissible ecclesiastical arbitration, which may be reviewed under BCO 43. The SJC did not reach the merits.
summary: Third Presbyterian Church asked the SJC to review Evangel Presbytery's denial of its complaint against a Presbytery commission's binding arbitration award of $57,000 to Covenant Classical School. The SJC ruled the complaint not judicially in order, not denied on the merits: PCA courts may not serve as civil arbitrators, and neither Presbytery nor the SJC may review legally binding arbitration judgments. Church courts may act only as ecclesiastical arbitrators, whose decisions lack civil effect and are reviewable under BCO 43. The complaint's five grounds were not reached.
